correctness.rationale: Correct arclength-centered Green evaluation norm equals F(x)/m-J/(2m^2), with F(x)=int R(x,y)ds. Exact unit-edge resistance interpolation gives edge quadratic F(x_t)=(1-t)F(u)+tF(v)+(m-1-mr(u,v))t(1-t). Vertex effective resistances from complete multipartite Laplacian eigen-decomposition yield B_i, J, alpha_ij. The positive profile comparison (formula 5) reduces global maximizers to two largest part classes. Formula 6 proves alpha_12-(B1-B2)>0 iff minimum combinatorial degree D>=3, including separate two-part, all-singleton and >=3-part bounds; D<=2 cases enumerate stars, two-part degree-two, tripartite degree-two, triangle and square. Equality in Green Cauchy-Schwarz classifies norming functions. Independent grounded-Laplacian exact rational computations reproduce vertex scores and sharp constants for eight configurations including both circle exceptions and K_(1,2,3), while infinite-parameter inequality follows analytically.

originality.rationale: Qualified surviving result is the global *explicit* complete-multipartite localization threshold at D=3, identification of edges joining two largest classes, exact off-midpoint t*, low-degree classification and equality functions across all part sizes. The full general arbitrary-metric-graph resistance-curvature envelope published same 2026-11-08 is strong broader background giving a finite computation for any input graph, and a second 2026-11-08 result already solves complete bipartite K_m,n for m,n>=3. These are NOT new special cases. Their statements do not explicitly classify the multipartite degree-threshold or prove the strict all-part-size ranking inequality; the new piece is a nontrivial closed and exhaustive parametric specialization. Das-Yang (2017) proves only vertex-to-vertex resistances, not continuum sharp arclength evaluations. Historical implicit derivation from general envelope remains substantial risk.
